intervals.label: proposed / design
intervals.note: No formal proposal or approval date is published. The start is taken as the August 2020 IceCube-Gen2 science white paper; the Technical Design Report followed in July 2023 (Parts I and II) and June 2024 (Part III), and the official pages still describe Gen2 as “proposed” and “under development”.
intervals.quote: While plans for this large-scale upgrade are under development, investigators have secured funding for mid-scale instrumentation advancements that will produce science results nearly a decade earlier than the full facility expansion.

intervals.label: planned operation
intervals.note: Schedule from the 2020 white paper, which also states construction will take 8 years and cost about $350M.
intervals.quote: Construction will take 8 years and cost about $350M. The goal is to have IceCube-Gen2 fully operational by 2033.

start.note: “The goal is to have IceCube-Gen2 fully operational by 2033” (2020 white paper); a schedule, not a commitment.

quantity.note: “about 8 cubic kilometers” on the official Beyond IceCube page.
quantity.quote: By roughly doubling the instrumentation already deployed, the telescope will see an increase in volume to about 8 cubic kilometers, aimed at roughly an order of magnitude increase in neutrino detection rates.

name: IceCube-Gen2
notes: Conflict with the task brief: the brief cited arXiv:2308.04141 as the IceCube-Gen2 TDR. That arXiv identifier is a 2-Higgs-doublet-model theory paper and is unrelated. The TDR is not on arXiv; it is published by the collaboration at icecube-gen2.wisc.edu (Parts I and II, July 2023; Part III, June 2024) and is recorded as document:icecube-gen2-technical-design-report.
No construction, approval or funding decision is published, so no approved/construction interval is recorded.

physics_goals.quote: An in-depth exploration of the neutrino universe requires a next-generation IceCube detector. Named IceCube-Gen2 and based on the robust design of the current detector, the goal for the new observatory is to deliver statistically significant samples of very high energy astrophysical neutrinos, in the PeV to EeV range.
physics_goals.value: Resolve the high-energy neutrino sky from TeV to EeV energies and deliver statistically significant samples of PeV–EeV astrophysical neutrinos

physics_goals.quote: IceCube-Gen2 is designed to: 1) Resolve the high-energy neutrino sky from TeV to EeV energies; 2) Investigate cosmic particle acceleration through multi-messenger observations; 3) Reveal the sources and propagation of the highest energy particles in the universe; 4) Probe fundamental physics with high-energy neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Investigate cosmic particle acceleration through multi-messenger observations

physics_goals.quote: 4) Probe fundamental physics with high-energy neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Probe fundamental physics with high-energy neutrinos

summary.plain: The planned successor to IceCube: about eight times the volume of ice, ten thousand light sensors and a huge radio antenna array, designed to catch many more neutrinos and the most energetic ones of all.
summary.technical: Proposed next-generation South Pole neutrino observatory: an optical array of ~8 km³ with ~10,000 sensors on 120 strings to 2,600 m depth and string spacing above 250 m, a surface array, and a ~500 km² in-ice radio array for EeV-scale neutrinos. Technical Design Report Parts I–II (July 2023) and Part III (June 2024); the 2020 white paper targets full operation by 2033.

unique_capabilities.quote: The incredible clarity of the Antarctic glacier, revealed by the construction and operation of IceCube, will allow the spacing between light sensors to exceed 250 meters, instead of the current 125 meters in IceCube.
unique_capabilities.value: An optical array of roughly 8 km³ instrumented volume obtained by increasing string spacing beyond 250 m

unique_capabilities.quote: Furthermore, through the addition of a radio array, IceCube-Gen2 will extend the energy range by several orders of magnitude compared to IceCube.
unique_capabilities.value: A ~500 km² in-ice radio array extending the energy reach by orders of magnitude beyond IceCube
